text:
alex: Noticing a spike in GPU attach failures in eu-west3 starting ~12:03 UTC. Correlating with NVMe metadata flush storms.

alex: Snippet:
```
kernel: nvme0n1: metadata flush burst, write latency > 200ms
checkpointd[2211]: flushed 18k meta entries in 1.1s
provisioner: attach timeout waiting for disk ready (EIO)
node: iostat -x nvme0: util=99% avgqu-sz=47 await=110.2
```

maya: Is this localized to a few hosts or wide-spread? Could be the cross-region model-sync kicked off.

alex: Early signs are multi-node in the same pool. The timing matches a bulk model-sync from apac -> eu-west3 and concurrent replica reconcile tasks.

devin: If metadata writes are synchronous and greedy they will drown user IO. Can we gate checkpointd or make it yield to the scheduler? We have a rate-limiter we can flip.

sre-bot: alert: gpu-attach-failure-eu-west3 count=34 severity=high

maya: Short-term options: 1) Bump checkpointd into background mode 2) Reduce model-sync concurrency 3) Move low-priority attaches to other pools. Which is least risky?

alex: Least risky: flip scheduler to mq-deadline on a canary and apply a soft meta-op rate limit. Historical precedent: scheduler change lowered write tail latency in 2 previous incidents.

ops-junior: Applied mq-deadline on gnode-eu-321 (canary). Attach successes went from 2/8 -> 7/8 in the first minute.

devin: I'll push a tiny checkpointd flag: `--meta-qps=400 --meta-backoff-ms=150` and emit metric `checkpointd_meta_qps`. Also add `meta_flush_p95`.

maya: Rolling the flag to 20% of eu-west3 now and reducing model-sync workers from 12 -> 4.

alex: Created a dashboard panel: /dash/storage/eu-west3 showing meta_qps, nvme_util, gpu_attach_fail_rate. Monitoring live.

ops-junior: Canary looks promising. NVMe util dropped from ~97% -> ~62% on canary hosts; attach failures ceased there.

maya: Rolling to 60% now. We'll keep model-sync throttled for the next 30m while we observe.

devin: Long-term proposals: separate metadata onto dedicated SSDs, enlarge in-memory metadata cache, or implement coordinated batched flush windows. Rough cost: dedicated tiny NVMe adds ~$0.018/node/hr but would prevent many P1s.

alex: Action items: Maya + Devin to run a staging test isolating metadata writes to a separate device; Ops-junior to add prometheus alerts for meta_qps > 800 and nvme_util > 90% sustained 1m; I'll schedule a postmortem slot tomorrow.

sre-bot: incident-bot: created INC-2026-1358 priority=P1

ops-junior: Pushed the rate-limit patch to checkpointd and deployed to remaining eu-west3 nodes. Metrics are reporting.

maya: Continued roll-out complete. Monitoring shows stable attach success and reduced write-latency tail. Filing follow-up ticket storage/ephemeral-meta-isolation.

alex: Closing operational thread. Postmortem draft to follow after 24h stable telemetry. Thanks all.
